pilot.summary: First game with the deck, a pod of three at home against Stuart (zombie tokens) and Steven (card draw and counterspells). Sol Ring in the opener got it going fast. Echo of Eons made Shabraz big and almost killed Stuart through commander damage. Then it went grindy. Brallin got removed twice and picked up tax, no more ramp showed up, and I had no removal for the board or answer to Steven's counters. No result was logged.

A loss at Oliver's, the second game of the night, with Oliver, Tom and Ryan. I mulliganed into a hand with one playable creature and a bunch of wheels and wasn't sure I should have kept it. The Shabraz wheels went well. The main finding is that the list runs too many wheels. They should be finishers held until both commanders are out and big, partly because the table doesn't like discarding its hand over and over.

read.what_it_does: No game has been played on v2.0.0, the voltron list merged 2026-10-24, so this read comes from two games on lists the deck no longer runs. On those lists the plan was to get both commanders out, then fire wheels so Brallin hits everyone for the discards and Shabraz grows off the draws, and win through commander damage with flying or trample from red mana. That is how it got closest to a win: Echo of Eons made Shabraz big and almost killed Stuart through commander damage (001), and the Shabraz wheels went well at Oliver's (002). The voltron rebuild keeps that commander-damage kill. Whether it plays out that way at a table has not been seen yet.
read.how_it_plays: Fast when the opening hand has the mana, and only then. Sol Ring in the opener made game 001 fast (001). After that the pair works like a nine-drop. Brallin at four and Shabraz at five, plus tax every time one gets removed, is the Ur-Dragon problem in Jeskai (001). The wheels are loud. The table either loved them or hated them (001), and repeated discards cost goodwill even in a pod where Oliver was also making people discard (002). In both games it ended up grinding: no removal to cut the board back and a counterspell seat to fight through (001), and a loss after a mulligan to a hand with one creature (002).
mindful_of: The commanders get removed and the tax stacks up. Brallin was taken out twice in 001 even with Lightning Greaves and boots protecting them. Lightning Greaves is still in v2.0.0 and played well (001).
Ramp past the opening hand felt light. Jeska's Will never showed up (001). Jeska's Will and Sol Ring are both still in the deck. v2.0.0 adds rocks, and that is untested at a table.
Don't fire a wheel just to fire it. In 001 I threw away really useful cards of my own because I just needed to do the wheel (001).
Wheels are finishers. Hold them until both commanders are out and already big, then chain one into the next with red open for trample (001, 002).
Think about the keep. In 002 I mulliganed to a hand with one playable creature and a bunch of wheels, and I still don't know if I should have kept it (002).

There was nothing to cut the board back with. In 001 I had no creature or enchantment removal when the board needed it, and Steven's counterspells made it a grind (001). Whether v2.0.0 fixes that hasn't been tested in a game.
Wheels cost goodwill. Making people discard their hand over and over is not something they enjoy (001, 002).
Downweight the goldfish on this deck. It doesn't see removal or interaction, and following it moves the deck in the wrong direction (002).
read.what_changed: Game 001 was on v1.2.0 and game 002 on v1.3.0. Nothing has been played on v2.0.0. Between them, v1.3.0 brought in Torbran and swapped in three wheels. Game 002 on that list said there were too many wheels (002). v2.0.0, the voltron merge, cut wheels: Echo of Eons, Magus of the Wheel, Time Reversal, Burning Inquiry and Teferi's Puzzle Box are gone, and Windfall stays. That goes straight at the too-many-wheels complaint from 002, but no game has tested it yet. Swiftfoot Boots, which was protecting the commanders in 001, is gone too. The voltron merge added equipment and other ways to protect them. Everything above is true of the deck it was read against. The first night on v2.0.0 is the one that tests it.
